residual_risks: The 5 skipped/erroring cases (interpreter-pin exactness and 5 live-PostgreSQL tests requiring the psycopg driver) are a pre-existing, already-documented local-venv gap unrelated to this task; a real PostgreSQL 16 IS live and reachable in this run (verified directly via pg_isready and a real wrong-password rejection over the compose network), but ocor-runtime/.venv has no psycopg installed, so ocor-runtime/tests/tasks/test_ocor_dev_0015.py's own live suite still cannot exercise it. Installing psycopg to close that specific gap is out of scope for this task and is noted as a distinct future opportunity now that real Docker infrastructure is confirmed available in this environment.

SPIRE bootstrap in this run used a freshly generated, disposable, non-committed self-signed CA and join token; this is a from-scratch bootstrap procedure that was not previously documented step-by-step anywhere in the repository (only the steady-state rotation flow in deploy/bootstrap/services/spire/qualify.py was), so a future rerun must reconstruct the same two-phase sequence (server up -> generate real join token -> agent up) rather than assume a persisted environment file.

This provisioning/health-check evidence does not qualify OCOR-DEV-0016/0017/0018 (the C3/C4-backend concurrency, exact-at-commit and marking-safe projection spikes), which remain separate, not-yet-run tasks.
rollback_procedure_verified: Executed bounded rollback/recovery for two independently-checked services (terminusdb, kafka): docker pause produced a typed DEGRADED status with a specific reason, docker unpause restored READY within the bounded window, and the full 11-container stack was confirmed healthy afterward with `docker compose ps`.
